articles.title: “My Bike, My Rules”: Bengaluru Biker Arrested After Road Rage Video Goes Viral
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: The Bengaluru City Police have arrested Sameer, a resident of Kadirenahalli, after a road rage incident in which he allegedly declared “my bike, my rules” following a near-accident at a busy city junction.

body.html:
The Bengaluru City Police have arrested Sameer, a resident of Kadirenahalli, after a road rage incident in which he allegedly declared “my bike, my rules” following a near-accident at a busy city junction.

The incident occurred at the Dickenson Road signal on January 26 (Republic Day), when Sameer allegedly jumped a traffic signal and nearly collided with a car driven by M.N. Praveen, a city resident.

According to the FIR, when Praveen questioned the traffic violation, the biker reacted aggressively, abused him verbally, and allegedly reached into the car through a partially open window and attempted to slap him, while also issuing threats.

The confrontation was recorded on Praveen’s mobile phone, and the video later went viral on X, drawing widespread public outrage. The footage shows the biker chasing the car briefly, attempting to hit the driver twice, as traffic piled up and other motorists honked.

Following the complaint and viral backlash, Commercial Street Police registered a case and arrested Sameer on charges related to assault, verbal abuse, and traffic violations.

Police said the case highlights the growing concern over road rage incidents in Bengaluru, particularly on congested city roads, and reiterated the need for strict enforcement of traffic rules to ensure public safety.

#Bengaluru #RoadRage #MyBikeMyRules #TrafficViolation #RepublicDay #PublicSafety #ViralVideo #BengaluruPolice #BreakingNews

articles.title: “Naked Man in Car Chases Woman”: Bengaluru Police Register Suo Motu Case After Viral Video
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A day after a disturbing video surfaced on social media, Hebbagodi police in Bengaluru have registered a suo motu case under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) over alleged sexual harassment.

body.html:
A day after a disturbing video surfaced on social media, Hebbagodi police in Bengaluru have registered a suo motu case under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) over alleged sexual harassment.

In the viral video, shared on the woman’s Instagram handle, she alleged that while returning home from work, a man sitting completely naked inside a car repeatedly called out to her and drove the vehicle towards her in a threatening manner. The woman is heard shouting for help and accusing passersby of ignoring her distress.

She further claimed that some people smiled and walked away, assuming the incident was part of a social media reel.

The case was registered based on a complaint filed by Rushabhendra, Head Constable at Hebbagodi police station, who came across the video during routine monitoring of social media. In his complaint, he stated that the footage clearly showed the woman accusing a man in a car of sexually harassing her while being in a disrobed state.

Police registered the case on Sunday and have launched an investigation. Efforts are underway to trace the accused using CCTV footage from the surrounding areas. The police are also trying to locate the woman to record her statement.

Further investigation is in progress, senior officials said.

#Bengaluru #Hebbagodi #ViralVideo #SexualHarassment #PublicSafety #WomenSafety #CCTVProbe #BreakingNews

articles.title: ₹18 Crore Inside Job? Domestic Help Pull Off One of Bengaluru’s Biggest Jewellery Heists
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A major theft has been reported from Bengaluru’s Marathahalli area, where gold, diamond, silver jewellery and cash worth around ₹18 crore were stolen from the residence of builder M R Shivakumar at ASK Lake Garden on Kempapura Main Road in Yamaluru.

body.html:
A major theft has been reported from Bengaluru’s Marathahalli area, where gold, diamond, silver jewellery and cash worth around ₹18 crore were stolen from the residence of builder M R Shivakumar at ASK Lake Garden on Kempapura Main Road in Yamaluru.

According to police, the accused are a Nepalese couple, Dinesh (32) and his wife Kamala (25), who had joined the household as domestic workers barely 20 days before the incident.

The theft took place between 9 am and 12.30 pm on January 25, when no family members were at home. Shivakumar was out of the country on a trip to the Philippines, while his son Shimanth S Arjun (28), along with his wife and mother, had gone to attend a land worship ceremony at H Cross on the Hoskote–Chintamani Road.

Arjun stated in his complaint that around 12.38 pm, the family’s cook Ambika informed him that cupboard locks had been broken and valuables stolen. When the family rushed back, they found lockers on both the ground floor and first floor forcibly opened using an iron bar.

Police said about 11.5 kg of gold and diamond jewellery, nearly 5 kg of silver ornaments and ₹11.5 lakh in cash were stolen, taking the total value of the theft to approximately ₹18 crore.

Investigations revealed that Kamala had allegedly taken another house help outside on a pretext, after which Dinesh reportedly called five to six accomplices to the house. The gang is suspected to have switched off the UPS and disconnected the power supply to disable CCTV cameras before executing the theft.

The accused couple were hired as replacements for the previous domestic staff, Vikash and Maya, who had worked at the house for nine months and had planned to return to their native place. Despite repeated requests, Dinesh and Kamala had not submitted identity proofs and had agreed to work for a monthly salary of ₹27,000.

Police suspect the involvement of a Nepalese gang and believe the crime was pre-planned, with the accused closely observing the family’s movements.

The Marathahalli Police have registered a case under Section 306 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (theft by clerk or servant) and formed multiple teams to trace the absconding accused. CCTV footage from nearby areas is being examined as efforts continue to recover the stolen valuables.

articles.title: Mumbai Horror: School Bus Crushes Grandmother and 9-Month-Old Baby in Khetwadi, Infant Killed
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A horrific accident shook Mumbai’s Khetwadi area on Tuesday (27 Jan 2026) afternoon when a school bus ran over a woman and her nine-month-old grandchild, killing the infant on the spot and leaving the woman critically injured.

body.html:
A horrific accident shook Mumbai’s Khetwadi area on Tuesday (27 Jan 2026) afternoon when a school bus ran over a woman and her nine-month-old grandchild, killing the infant on the spot and leaving the woman critically injured.

The incident occurred around 12.23 pm when the woman had gone to pick up her granddaughter, a student of JB Soman School, Colaba, from the school bus drop-off point.

CCTV footage shows the young girl alighting from the bus, after which the woman, carrying the infant in her arms, holds the child’s hand and attempts to cross the road in front of the bus. Moments later, the bus starts moving.

The visuals capture the woman bracing for impact as she, the infant, and the schoolgirl fall to the ground. The front right wheel of the bus runs over the woman and the infant, narrowly missing the granddaughter by just centimetres. The child can be seen crawling away to safety, while a scooter rider stops just in time to avoid hitting her.

The infant died on the spot, while the woman sustained serious injuries and was rushed to hospital. Passersby immediately rushed to help.

Police said a case has been registered and the bus driver has been arrested. Further investigation is underway.

#MumbaiAccident #Khetwadi #SchoolBusCrash #CCTVFootage #RoadSafety #ChildSafety #MumbaiNews #TragicIncident

articles.title: Love, Lies and Lethal Injections: Nurse Daughter Kills Parents Over Inter-Caste Marriage Dispute
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shocking double murder has come to light in Vikarabad district of Telangana, where a young woman allegedly killed her own parents after they opposed her love marriage with a youth she met on Instagram.

body.html:
A shocking double murder has come to light in Vikarabad district of Telangana, where a young woman allegedly killed her own parents after they opposed her love marriage with a youth she met on Instagram.

The accused has been identified as Nakka Surekha, a resident of Yacharam village in Bantwaram mandal. She works as a nurse at a private nursing home.

According to police, Surekha had been in a relationship for the past two years with a youth she met through Instagram. However, her parents refused to accept the marriage as it was an inter-caste relationship. Angered by their opposition, Surekha allegedly planned their murder.

Police said the accused brought anaesthesia and sedative drugs from the nursing home where she worked. She reportedly told her parents that the injections were medicines for body pain and administered high-dose sedatives, which led to their deaths.

After the incident, Surekha informed her brother that both parents had died a natural death. However, suspicion arose, following which police conducted an investigation.

During questioning, Surekha allegedly confessed to murdering her parents. A case has been registered, and the accused has been taken into police custody. Further investigation is underway.

articles.title: Gunpoint Robbery in Bengaluru: Jewellers Looted Near Dasanapura, Minor Son Injured #breakingnews
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A daring daylight robbery was reported at Ramdev Jewellers near the Dasanapura bus stand in Nelamangala, on the outskirts of Bengaluru, late Tuesday evening, leaving the shop owner’s family shaken and a minor injured.

body.html:
A daring daylight robbery was reported at Ramdev Jewellers near the Dasanapura bus stand in Nelamangala, on the outskirts of Bengaluru, late Tuesday evening, leaving the shop owner’s family shaken and a minor injured.

According to police, the incident occurred around 5.30 pm when three unidentified assailants arrived on a two-wheeler and barged into the jewellery store. One of the accused allegedly brandished what appeared to be a pistol and threatened the staff.

At the time of the incident, the shop owner, Manik Raman, was not present, and the shop was being managed by his two sons. When they attempted to resist, a scuffle broke out, during which one of the sons, a minor, sustained injuries.

The robbers fled the spot within minutes. As per the complaint lodged at Madanayakanahalli police station, the accused escaped with around 30 grams of gold ornaments and ₹50,000 in cash.

Police have registered a case and formed multiple teams to trace the culprits. CCTV footage from the shop and nearby areas is being examined to track the escape route of the motorcycle.

D.L. Nagesh, Deputy Commissioner of Police, North West Division, said the police are verifying whether the weapon used was a real firearm or a replica and added that several leads have been obtained.

articles.title: ‘MLA’ Sticker Car Mows Down Bikers at 150 kmph in UP: Minister’s Son Named in FIR
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A speeding Fortuner car bearing an “MLA” sticker crushed three bike riders in Uttar Pradesh’s Lalitpur district, killing one youth and leaving two others critically injured. The incident occurred late Monday night in Barkhera village under the Jakhlon police station limits.

body.html:
A speeding Fortuner car bearing an “MLA” sticker crushed three bike riders in Uttar Pradesh’s Lalitpur district, killing one youth and leaving two others critically injured. The incident occurred late Monday night in Barkhera village under the Jakhlon police station limits.

According to police and villagers, the Fortuner was allegedly travelling at around 150 kmph when it rammed into the motorcycle around midnight and dragged the victims nearly 300 metres. Shivendra (20) died on the spot, while Anuj (20) and Shankar (45) sustained serious injuries and are undergoing treatment.

Investigations revealed that the Fortuner is registered in the name of the wife of UP minister Manohar Lal Panth. It is alleged that the vehicle was being driven by the minister’s son, Naresh Panth, at the time of the accident. An FIR has been registered against him.

Locals said the car had an MLA sticker and an assembly pass displayed. The impact was so severe that the vehicle was badly damaged, with parts scattered across the road, and its airbags deployed. Five people were reportedly inside the car.

After the collision, the occupants allegedly abandoned the vehicle and fled. Villagers claimed that when they tried to stop them, the accused threatened them with a pistol before escaping. Liquor bottles and disposable cups were also reportedly found inside the car.

Angered by the incident, locals blocked the road demanding action, but later dispersed after assurances from the police. Authorities have launched a detailed investigation to establish responsibility and are examining all evidence.
Attempts to contact the minister for his response were unsuccessful.

#Lalitpur #UttarPradesh #RoadAccident #MLACar #MinisterSon #HitAndRun #Speeding #JusticeForVictims #UPPolice
